questions.key_step: Sum of 64 terms = 7 x sum of odd-placed terms; cancel (1-r^64), get 1+r=7
questions.justification: Direct GP formulas for two sums; one cancellation; options available.

questions.key_step: A satisfies the given cubic, so compare with its characteristic polynomial: b+5=4, a-5b-1=-1
questions.justification: Expand one 3x3 characteristic polynomial and match coefficients; routine but long, and the identification needs Cayley-Hamilton.

questions.key_step: sin(theta)+sin(theta+2pi/3)+sin(theta+4pi/3)=0 gives 1/x+1/y+1/z=0, so xy+yz+zx=0 and trace != 0; statement II is vacuous
questions.justification: Hidden trig identity plus an adjoint-of-adjoint formula; the logical trap in statement II (false antecedent) is where students slip.

questions.key_step: adj(X^-1)=X/|X|, then (XYZ)^-1 reverses the order
questions.justification: Standard adjoint/inverse identities chained for 3-4 steps; no insight beyond the identities.

questions.key_step: b=2a-3 from the AP and (a-1)^2=3(b+1) from the GP, reject a=1
questions.justification: Two short relations, one quadratic; options available.

questions.key_step: |2A|^3=2^9|A|^3 so |A|=16 and alpha^2-beta^2=16 over integers
questions.justification: Short chain: det scaling then an integer difference-of-squares search with options.

questions.key_step: D=0 gives lambda=5, Dx=0 gives mu=9, then distance from (5,9) to 4x-3y=0
questions.justification: Two determinants then a distance formula; routine multi-stage.

questions.key_step: Solve in terms of z=k, then integrality forces k=3 mod 17, count within 7<=x+y+z<=77
questions.justification: Needs a divisibility argument on a parametrised solution, not just a routine determinant; easy to miscount.
Row-reduce a 3x3 and apply the adjoint-power rule; routine.

questions.key_step: T_n=S_n-S_{n-1} factorises to (2n-1)(2n+1)(2n+3)/8, then 1/T_n telescopes
questions.justification: Standard difference-of-sums then telescoping; clean but mechanical.

questions.key_step: Same as Q8: parametrise by z=k and count integer solutions with the sum bound
questions.justification: Same counting and divisibility step as Q8; duplicate of that question.

questions.key_step: Delta=0 and Delta_3=0 give alpha=-19/9, beta=6/11
questions.justification: Two 3x3 determinants and a pair of linear equations; routine.

questions.key_step: Same as Q7: D=0 gives lambda=5 and Dx=0 gives mu=9, then tangent circle radius
questions.justification: Duplicate of Q7; routine two-determinant chain.

questions.key_step: A^2=I because M^T M=1, so eigenvalues are +1 and -1
questions.justification: Short once A^2=I is seen; also needs both eigenvalues to be attained.

questions.key_step: Cramer's rule with both x<0 and y<0 gives (-15/2,0), then integrate the linear |A|
questions.justification: Two routine stages (inequalities then a linear integral).

questions.key_step: 1+4r^4=(2r^2-2r+1)(2r^2+2r+1) turns T_r into a telescoping difference
questions.justification: Needs the Sophie Germain factorisation, which students rarely see unprompted; then standard telescoping.

questions.key_step: XᵀAX=0 for all X forces A skew-symmetric; solve for entries; det(adj(2(A+I)))=|2(A+I)|^2
questions.justification: Several linked ideas (skew-symmetry from a quadratic form, solving from two images, adjoint determinant); moderate length.

questions.key_step: Nth term (n^2+3n-2)/2 from three terms, then 4alpha-beta collapses to a cubic
questions.justification: Fit a quadratic and sum polynomial powers; routine but arithmetic heavy.

questions.key_step: D=0 gives lambda=1,-1/3,-2/3 (and each must be checked to give no solution)
questions.justification: One determinant and a consistency check for each root; routine.

questions.key_step: Sum the first row over k (linearity), then R2-R1, R3-R1 make the determinant triangular
questions.justification: Linearity of a determinant in a row; neat but a single trick.
